title: Tenant guidance for latency spike — concise update & mitigation steps
content:
Purpose:

This is a concise customer-facing draft intended for tenants and partner integrators that experienced increased request latency and occasional truncated streaming responses between 2028-06-09 17:35 UTC and 2028-06-10 02:12 UTC. The doc mixes a short status-page-ready blurb, recommended tenant actions (minimal, low-friction), an executive-style summary for account teams, and a post-incident follow-up checklist.

Important: keep messaging short on the status page. Use the short template below for the live status entry; use the longer template for emailed tenant postmortems or account-manager handoffs.

---

STATUS PAGE SHORT ENTRY (one-line + 2-sentence follow-up):

Title: Investigating increased inference latency in us-west-2

Message (short): We experienced elevated inference latency for a subset of requests in us-west-2 between 2028-06-09 17:35 UTC and 2028-06-10 02:12 UTC. Traffic routing changes and a service-side cache warm-up regression caused slower responses for long-tail requests; a rollback and targeted cache priming reduced latency to normal levels.

Suggested status tags: degraded_performance, resolved

---

CONCISE TENANT ACTIONS (what customers should do now):

1) If you observed user-facing timeouts or truncated streaming, retry logic with exponential backoff is recommended; increase client-side per-request timeout by +2s temporarily while we finish verification.
2) If you rely on per-tenant KV cache priming (custom warm-up), trigger a quick rewarm for high-QPS routes (example: POST /v1/generate with role=assistant) — we will provide an automated rewarm tool in follow-up for high-volume tenants.
3) For critical integrations that cannot tolerate retries, switch the route to the dedicated capacity model (if subscribed) via the Console toggle — CS/SE can assist (see contact below).

Note to tenant engineers: we do NOT recommend changing model parameters (temperature/top_p) to mitigate latency; that will not help. Batching and shorter max_tokens will reduce average latency but affect throughput/quality tradeoffs — coordinate with us before altering production prompts.

---

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY FOR ACCOUNT TEAMS (2–3 bullets):

- Impact: ~2.4% of requests in us-west-2 experienced >1500ms latency spikes; 0.06% experienced truncated streaming segments. No data loss.
- Cause (short): A routing rule push intended to reduce cross-AZ tails combined with a regression in cache eviction heuristics that increased cold-KV-cache misses for long-tail sequences.
- Resolution: Rolled back the routing change at 02:00 UTC and applied a targeted cache rewarm; telemetry returned to baseline by 02:12 UTC.

---

DETAILED CUSTOMER-FACING POSTMORTEM (draft):

What happened:
Between 2028-06-09 17:35 UTC and 2028-06-10 02:12 UTC, customers sending multipart streaming requests and requests with long prefix sequences in region us-west-2 saw intermittent increases in end-to-end latency. A small subset of high-sequence-length requests experienced truncated chunked responses when server-side timeouts were reached.

Scope and impact:
- Affected scope: requests routed to the new per-AZ routing policy in us-west-2 (approx 18% of total us-west-2 traffic during the window).
- Customer impact: Visible slowdowns for interactive chat sessions and longer generation jobs; best-effort retries resolved most sessions. Enterprise Dedicated customers with pinned routes were largely unaffected.
- Metrics: Peak 99th-percentile token latency rose from 420ms to 1.9s; request error rate (5xx) increased from 0.02% to 0.18% at peak.

Root cause analysis (customer-facing, non-sensitive):
- Primary chain: An automated routing tweak intended to reduce network tail latency caused a subset of requests to be sent to newer hosts that had an updated cache-eviction tuning. The eviction tuning introduced more aggressive KV cache churn for keys with long prefix patterns. That produced elevated cold-cache misses for long-tail sequences and caused the runtime to perform additional model KV reloads, increasing token generation latency beyond client timeouts in some cases.
- Contributing factors: insufficient pre-deployment traffic-shaped load tests for the combination of routing policy + recent eviction heuristic; monitoring did not have a dedicated alert for per-route cold-cache miss rate.

What we fixed and why it works:
1) Immediate rollback of the routing change (2028-06-10 02:00 UTC) to restore normal host selection.
2) Targeted cache rewarm for frequently seen long-prefix keys to reduce cold misses.
3) Reverted the eviction tuning; a new tuning will be rolled forward behind a canary with synthetic long-prefix traffic.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2028-06-09 17:35 — Change deployed: per-AZ routing policy pushed (canary fraction 20%).
- 2028-06-09 18:05 — Initial uptick in 99p latency observed by internal dashboards.
- 2028-06-09 19:20 — On-call paged; SRE begins investigation (sev-2).
- 2028-06-09 23:10 — Root-cause hypothesis: increased KV cache churn; mitigation options discussed.
- 2028-06-10 01:58 — Decision to rollback routing change to stop additional exposure.
- 2028-06-10 02:00 — Routing rollback executed.
- 2028-06-10 02:06 — Targeted cache rewarm completed for flagged tenants/routes.
- 2028-06-10 02:12 — Metrics returned to baseline; incident declared mitigated.

Follow-up actions (what tenants should expect next):
- Within 48 hours: We will publish a follow-up note with per-tenant telemetry where available (top-affected routes) and a recommended rewarm script for tenants to run if they saw degraded UX.
- Within 7 days: A staged re-introduction of the improved routing policy behind a synthetic long-prefix workload canary and new monitoring checks for per-route cold-cache miss rate.
- Within 30 days: Service release including improved eviction heuristics and an automated cache priming tool for large tenants.

Compensation / credits:
- Customers who can demonstrate user-facing impact (error/timeout windows + business impact) will be eligible for a one-time service credit. Account teams should gather evidence and open a CS ticket referencing INC-8543.

Status page templates (copy-paste):
- Short (for live status page):
Investigating elevated latency in us-west-2. We are rolling back a routing update and applying cache fixes; some tenants may see retries for in-progress requests.

- Full (customer email / partner message):
Subject: Incident summary — elevated inference latency in us-west-2 (2028-06-09)
Body: [Short summary] + [Impact and timeline above summarized] + [Tenant actions and contact info]. Keep it under 300 words.

Escalation and contacts:
- Primary CS lead: Dana Liu (dana@redwood.ai)
- SRE on-call: Ethan Brooks (pager, slack #sre-oncall)
- Solutions eng (for Dedicated migrations): Sofia Martinez (se@redwood.ai)

Open questions / TODOs (internal):
- Which large tenants saw the highest cold-cache miss rate? (Action: telemetry query: per-tenant cold-cache-rate by route — assigned to Ravi)
- Build a lightweight per-route synthetic canary generator for long-prefix sequences — assigned to applied-ml team (Maya / Ravi).
- Draft automated reheating tool and docs for Console-run rewarm — product + devexp.

Notes to account managers (how to use this doc):
- Use the Short status-page message verbatim for updates.
- For tenant emails, use the Full template and insert specific per-tenant metrics we will provide in the follow-up. Be empathetic: acknowledge the user impact, outline steps taken, and provide a clear contact for remediation and credits.

Appendix: technical detail snippets (optional for technical customers)
- Eviction heuristic change: moved from TTL-based conservative retention to adaptive LRU with epoch-based sliding window; increased churn for long-prefix keys.
- Mitigation approach: throttle eviction for keys flagged by sequence-length heuristics; pre-populate KV shards during rewarm to reduce on-demand reload penalties.

---

Draft version notes / provenance:

End of draft.
